newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah firms, offshore unloads swaps.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah firms, offshore unloads swaps.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah firmed against the dollar and swap premiums fell on offshore selling in moderate early trading on Thursday, dealers said.
One Japanese bank dealer said rupiah liquidity appeared to be sufficient and did not affect its value against the dollar.
"But we have seen plenty of swaps selling from offshore operators this morning. It seems they are comfortable with the rupiah."

Dealers said a calmer market in the region seemed to help operators regain confidence. Swap rates rose on Wednesday on offshore purchases after the ringgit and the peso were attacked by currency speculators.

Economists said a relatively strong economic fundamentals seemed to have helped protect the rupiah from speculators looking for victims after recent attacks on the Thai baht, the Phillipines peso and the Malaysian ringgit.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,432.0/32.3 at 0235 GMT against an opening of 2,432.3/32.8. Tomorrow and today rupiah were quoted at 2,430.5/31.4 and 2,430.5/31.0, respectively.
Some dealers said there was still some speculation in the market of a widening of the central bank intervention band which seemed to sustain upward pressure on the rupiah.
Overnight rupiah fell to 10.0 percent and overnight swap was at 0.30/0.38 points. Tom/next was at 0.85/0.90.
One-month swaps eased to 13.5/14.0 from 14.0/14.5 on Wednesday, three to 42.0/43.0 from 44.5/45.5 and six to 86.0/87.0 from 88.0/89.5 points.
The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,429/2,621 and the conversion band at 2,429/2,477 on Wednesday.
